messages.subject: new approach using plyr
parts:
Hello,

I am trying the plyr package to accomplish the task below:

My data(NPB) look like this:

str(NPB)
'data.frame': 238 obs. of 4 variables:

Treatment Fish Time Se_conc
1 Selenate 1 0.0 0.01145679
2 Selenate 1 1.5 0.04358848
3 Selenate 1 3.0 0.08335803
4 Selenate 1 6.0 0.13076543
5 Selenate 1 12.0 0.19055144
6 Selenate 1 24.0 0.08691358
7 Selenate 1 48.0 0.04503704
8 Selenate 2 0.0 0.01700000

I can use the following code for 1 Treatment/Fish combo:

auc(conc=NPB[1:7,4],time=NPB[1:7,3])

The desired result is:


AUC AUMC
observed 4.669827 88.25896
interpolated NA NA
infinity 5.847050 175.53712

Now, I have 33 other Treatment/Fish combinations that I need to run
the "auc" function on and produce a summary table.

Note: the last treatment only has 4 fish; the other 6 treatments have
5 fish

So, I am trying to use the "plyr" package; without success.

any thoughts,

Josh

I can use the following code for 1 Treatment/Fish combo:

auc(conc=NPB[1:7,4],time=NPB[1:7,3])

Question: where does the auc function come from? There are several such tests in various
packages on CRAN, but it appears that the one in package epicalc is tailor-made for this
problem:

> args(auc)
function (conc, time, id = NULL),

where id designates the grouping factor, although I can't see why it couldn't take more
than one group...If it does, you don't need to use plyr, at least for the AUC.

To do it the plyr way,  it would appear that you want dlply; since you are outputting a
matrix or data frame at each iteration, your output needs to be a list structure. Something like

dlply(NPB, .(Treatment, Fish), summarize, auc(Conc_se, Time))

Afterward, you can post-process it, perhaps with some combination of ldply, melt and cast;
it's hard to say because you don't specify what your desired end result is after the 34 combinations
have been processed.

HTH,
Dennis

any thoughts,

Josh

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: new approach using plyr
parts:
Try

dlply(NPB, .(Treatment, Fish), summarize, auc(Se_conc, Time)$est)

and make sure that each of your treatment/fish combinations have more than
one observation. You'll probably get some extra information about attributes,
but that shouldn't be a problem. What should matter is that each component of
the list is a data frame. In addition, the name of each list component is
of the form Treatment.Fish. You haven't said how you wanted to 'summarize'
the results, though, so whether this approach is best for your data, I can't tell.

HTH,
Dennis

parts:
Hadley,

Your hint was received and addressed ;-)))


I put a reproducible example below that needs to summarized with the
following columns:treatment, fish, AUCobs, AUMCobs, AUCinf,AUMCinf ---
without the rows of NA's----

#Reproducible example

npb_rep=data.frame(treatment=rep(1:7,each=35),
fish=rep(letters[1:5],each=7,length.out=245),
time=rep(0:6,length.out=245),conc=rep(rnorm
(7,mean=2.5),length.out=245));head(npb_rep,18);tail(npb_rep,18)

#Take off last treatment/fish combo

npb_rep=npb_rep[-c(239:245),];tail(npb_rep,18)


thanks in advance,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: new approach using plyr
parts:
Hi Josh,

Have a look at this code:

library(plyr)
library(PK)

npb_rep <- data.frame(
treatment = rep(1:7, each = 35),
fish = rep(letters[1:5], each = 7, length.out = 245),
time = rep(0:6, length.out = 245),
conc = rep(rnorm(7, mean = 2.5), length.out = 245));
#Take off last treatment/fish combo

npb_rep <- npb_rep[-c(239:245), ]

# Figure out how to get the output we want
one <- subset(npb_rep, treatment == 1 & fish == "a")
auc_one <- with(one, auc(time, conc))
auc_one

str(auc_one)
auc_one$est

# Do it for all of them
ddply(npb_rep, .(treatment, fish), function(df) {
with(df, auc(conc, time))$est
})


Regards,

Hadley
